reels.title: Price is a message
reels.srt:
1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:03,400
 Your price tells people what to expect

2
00:00:03,400 --> 00:00:06,700
 before you have said a word about the work.

3
00:00:06,700 --> 00:00:10,100
 If it is too low, they wonder what is wrong.

4
00:00:10,100 --> 00:00:13,300
 If it is a little higher than they thought,

5
00:00:13,300 --> 00:00:16,300
 they lean in. So choose it on purpose.

principles.name: Price the outcome
principles.description: Charge for what the work changes for the buyer, not for the hours it takes.
steps: Name the result the buyer wants
Put a number on what that result is worth to them
Set the price as a fair share of that number
red_flags: Pricing by the hour because it feels safe
Matching someone else's price without a reason of your own
green_flags: A price you can explain in one sentence
Buyers asking what is included, not what it costs
decision_criteria: Does the price say what the work is worth?
Could you say it out loud without apologising?
principles.example_application: A baker who sells wedding cakes prices by the celebration the cake serves, not by the hours in the kitchen.
verbatim_key_phrases: What is it worth to them?

principles.name: Say the price first
principles.description: Name the number early in a conversation, so that the rest of it can be about fit and not about waiting for the cost.
steps: Say the price in the first few minutes
Stop talking and let it land
Ask whether it works for them, then move to what would make it a yes
red_flags: Circling for ten minutes before the number comes up
Softening the price with an apology
green_flags: The buyer asks about the work after hearing the price
A no that comes early and costs nobody anything
decision_criteria: Has the buyer heard the number yet?
Is the next question about fit?
principles.example_application: A service provider states the price in the first call, asks whether it works, and spends the rest of the call on what would make it a yes.

principles.name: Check one number each week
principles.description: Choose the one number that says whether the business is healthy, look at it on the same day every week, and change one thing at a time.
steps: Pick the one number that matters most this quarter
Change one thing, then watch the number for a month
red_flags: Tracking ten numbers and acting on none
green_flags: This week's number can be said without looking it up
Each change has a before and an after
decision_criteria: Will this number move if the work is done well?
Is there one thing to change this week?
principles.example_application: The owner of a small shop watches the number of returning customers each Monday and tries one new thing a month to raise it.

reelsToFilm.words: Your price tells people what to expect before you have said a word about the work.
reelsToFilm.why: It was said more than any other point, and it stands alone.

reelsToFilm.idea: The day after you raise a price
reelsToFilm.words: The day after you raise a price, change nothing. Same warmth, same work, same you.
reelsToFilm.why: A calming note that belongs to no one principle.
